_note: DESIGN.md: Hottest of the HOT makeover / hair-salon / get-ready-for-the-fashion-show chains, Day of the Tentacle-style chained tasks across the ship, with the judged, passive-aggressive framing (control dressed as care; Story Structure Camera 2). Station and task text is written for the game in the sources' voice (no source text exists for the salon). A task: {id, station, text, needs: [item ids held and consumed], requires: [task ids done], gives: item id, outfit: {slot: part_id} applied to the paper doll}. items maps item id to its display name. When every task is done the passenger goes on to the show.

tasks.text: Open the envelope under your door: the Hottest of the HOT call sheet, with a note that says 'We only want you to feel your best (we noticed)'.
Put on the complimentary robe. It is one size, which is fine, for most.
Stand at the mirror the stewards hung a little too low. Find something about yourself that's positive and celebrate it. They will be along to help with the rest.
Show the purser your call sheet. She finds you a Glow Lounge appointment: 'a cancellation, you're so lucky, honestly, you looked like you needed it'.
Ask for your dress. The purser writes you a laundry claim tag and tells you, kindly, that white is a very confident choice.
Choose a ribbon from the 'Be a Bigger Yourself' display. The clerk says the red one is very brave and would really draw the eye away.
Hand over your claim tag. The attendant presses the white dress and pins on a card: 'size not final'.
Take the chair. The stylist asks, with real concern, who has been doing your hair. A trim, just to make it more manageable.
Let her put your hair up with the ribbon. 'A braid hides so much. It's a compliment, hold still.'
Change into the white dress. It fits the way these things fit when someone else chose the size.
Join the warm-up on the Lido. Everyone is rooting for you, and one by one they tell you so, and sign your card.
Give the stage manager your stamp and your card. She pins your runway number on with the bow, so nobody looks at anything else.
